title: Moses Springer Community Centre retrofit contract awarded
subtitle: Facility greenhouse gas progress, honoraria policy, accessibility committee refresh, Platinum bicycle award and THEMUSEUM update
overview: Council awarded the contract for the Moses Springer Community Centre energy, accessibility and retrofit project to Jackman Construction Ltd. for a total of $2,786,326.58 {{vote:m4}}. Staff said construction should start within weeks and finish by the end of May next year, so pool operations can resume in summer 2027. The work adds a universal washroom, an accessible path to the pool deck, a second accessible exit and new heating, cooling and dehumidification systems.

Council also accepted a progress report on greenhouse gas reductions at City facilities {{vote:m3}}, approved a revised Honoraria and Reimbursement Policy {{vote:m2}}, and approved refreshed Terms of Reference for the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee, with staff to recruit members {{vote:m5}}. Staff said the honoraria budget increase mainly reflects a revised cost-sharing arrangement with the Region for the accessibility committee and better tracking.

Council heard from THEMUSEUM on its attendance and finances, and was told Waterloo has earned a Platinum Bicycle Friendly Community designation. Council met in closed session on the disposition of City-owned lands, and the minutes record no public decision from it. For residents, the decisions mean upgraded recreation facilities, lower building emissions and a continuing regional approach to accessibility advice.

decisions.item: Moses Springer Community Centre retrofit contract
decisions.detail: Council awarded RFT26-12 to Jackman Construction Ltd. for a total of $2,786,326.58 including unrecoverable HST and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the agreement {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.item: City facilities greenhouse gas emissions update
decisions.detail: Council approved report COM2026-029 and recognized progress on emission reductions and successful grant applications supporting City energy and infrastructure projects {{vote:m3}}.
Council approved report CORP2026-035 and the revised Honoraria and Reimbursement Policy (A-042) {{vote:m2}}.
Council approved refreshed Terms of Reference, directed staff to recruit members for the new committee and to keep collaborating with other accessibility committees across the region {{vote:m5}}.

debate: On the honoraria policy, one councillor supported standardizing honoraria across divisions but asked why projected costs rose from a few thousand dollars to a possible annual figure far higher. Staff said the main driver is the revised regional partnership for the accessibility committee, with costs split between the City and Region, plus better tracking of amounts once paid from project budgets.

On greenhouse gas reductions, councillors asked about cybersecurity of building automation systems and about reliance on natural gas and the provincial electricity grid. Staff said the building controls run on a separate network with restricted remote access, and that grid emissions may rise in the short term, which could affect projected savings.

Councillors asked about rooftop solar. Staff said some sites could support it, some need roof structural work first, and installation could be City-owned or through a third-party power purchase agreement. Staff agreed to follow up on the funding still needed for future projects.

On the accessibility committee, one councillor worried that members from townships might not get issues communicated and acted on, since not every municipality will be at the table. Staff said communication links are still being designed, the membership offer was intentionally left open, and changes can come back to Council.

On Moses Springer, one councillor supported the project but noted an ongoing community need for shared space for gathering and preparing food in that part of the city, saying it should stay in mind for future planning.
